Title: Participation in the Finnish low-dose CT screening pilot by deprivation quintile
Authors: Esimerkki A; Esimerkki Ä; Dæmi Þ
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Respiratory Medicine, Example University Hospital, Tampere, Finland; 2. Faculty of Medicine, Example University, Helsinki, Finland
Background: Screening benefit depends on who attends.
Methods: Invitation and attendance records were linked to area deprivation quintiles for 18 400 invitees.
Results: Attendance fell from 62% in the least deprived quintile to 38% in the most deprived.
Conclusions: Uniform invitation does not produce uniform attendance.

Title: Radiologist workload in a Nordic screening programme
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Radiology, Example University Hospital, Copenhagen, Denmark
Methods: Prospective time-and-motion study across three reading sites.
Results: Median reading time was 4.8 minutes per baseline scan and 2.1 minutes per incidence scan.
Conclusions: Incidence rounds are cheaper to read than baseline rounds.

Title: Brock, Herder and Mayo models compared in a Nordic nodule cohort
Authors: Eksempel N; Dæmi B; Esimerkki A
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Pulmonary Medicine, Example University Hospital, Bergen, Norway; 2. Example National Hospital, Reykjavik, Iceland
Background: Guideline thresholds assume a calibrated model.
Methods: Three models were applied to 1 210 incidentally found nodules, with calibration assessed in deciles.
Results: All three discriminated well but over-predicted risk above 10%.
Conclusions: Discrimination and calibration disagree at the threshold that matters.

Title: Gap population after pathway change
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Pulmonary Medicine, Example University Hospital, Tampere, Finland
Background: A changed threshold moves patients in both directions.
Methods: Synthetic cohort sandbox with paired pathway assignment.
Results: Of 2 000 simulated patients, 7.4% changed arm and 2.1% moved to no follow-up.
Conclusions: The size of the gap population should be reported with any pathway change.

Title: Consolidation immunotherapy uptake across four Nordic countries
Authors: Exempel Ö; Eksempel Ø; Eksempel P; Esimerkki A; Esimerkki Ä
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden; 2. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark
Background: Uptake of consolidation therapy varies between health systems.
Results: Uptake ranged from 44% to 81% between countries.
Conclusions: Country of treatment predicted consolidation more strongly than performance status.

Title: Toxicity of concurrent chemoradiotherapy in patients over 75
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Odense, Denmark
Background: Older patients are under-represented in pivotal trials.
Results: Grade 3 or worse oesophagitis occurred in 21% of patients over 75 and 14% below.
Conclusions: Age alone did not predict treatment discontinuation.

Title: SBRT versus surgery for stage I NSCLC in operable patients
Authors: Dæmi B; Eksempel N; Eksempel Ø
Affiliations: 1. Example National Hospital, Reykjavik, Iceland; 2. Dept of Thoracic Surgery, Example University Hospital, Oslo, Norway
Background: Treatment choice in operable patients remains contested.
Results: Three-year overall survival was 78% after surgery and 71% after SBRT.
Conclusions: Residual confounding by comorbidity cannot be excluded from registry data.

Title: Lymph node upstaging after minimally invasive lobectomy
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Thoracic Surgery, Example University Hospital, Helsinki, Finland
Background: Nodal upstaging is a surrogate for surgical quality.
Results: Upstaging was 11.2% after VATS and 13.9% after open surgery.
Conclusions: The difference narrowed in centres with more than 60 procedures per year.

Title: Turnaround time for reflex NGS testing in four Nordic laboratories
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Pathology, Example National Hospital, Reykjavik, Iceland
Background: Treatment start depends on molecular results.
Results: Median turnaround was 11 days with an interquartile range of 8 to 17 days.
Conclusions: Turnaround varied more within laboratories than between them.

Title: PD-L1 scoring agreement between Nordic pathologists
Authors: Eksempel Ø; Dæmi Þ; Eksempel N
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Pathology, Example University Hospital, Copenhagen, Denmark
Methods: Twelve pathologists scored 60 blinded slides twice.
Results: Agreement at the 50% cut-off was moderate with kappa 0.58.
Conclusions: Agreement was lowest in the 1-49% band.

Title: Early palliative referral and place of death
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Tampere, Finland
Background: Place of death is used as a quality indicator.
Results: Referral more than 90 days before death was associated with death outside hospital in 64% versus 41%.
Conclusions: Association is not causal; referral timing reflects prognosis.

Title: Patient-reported outcomes collected by app during systemic therapy
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden
Results: Weekly completion was 71% at eight weeks and 52% at 16 weeks.
Conclusions: Completion falls as treatment continues; reminders alone did not hold it.

Title: Time from referral to treatment start across Nordic lung cancer pathways
Authors: Esimerkki A; Eksempel Ø; Dæmi B; Eksempel N; Exempel Ö
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Respiratory Medicine, Example University Hospital, Tampere, Finland; 2. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Copenhagen, Denmark
Results: Median referral-to-treatment was 41 days with a range of 29 to 58 between countries.
Conclusions: Target definitions differ enough to make direct comparison misleading.

Title: Time from referral to treatment start across Nordic lung cancer pathways
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark
Background: Submitted separately by a second group on the same indicator.
Methods: Audit of 420 consecutive referrals in one region.
Conclusions: Single-region audits and registry comparisons answer different questions.

Title: Lung cancer incidence in never-smokers in the Nordic countries 1995-2024
Affiliations: 1. Faculty of Medicine, Example University, Helsinki, Finland
Background: Never-smoker lung cancer is reported to be rising.
Methods: Nordic cancer registry data with smoking status from survey linkage.
Results: Age-standardised incidence in never-smoking women rose from 4.1 to 6.8 per 100 000.
Conclusions: Part of the rise may reflect improved smoking-status recording.

Title: Occupational asbestos exposure and mesothelioma trends
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Occupational Medicine, Example University Hospital, Bergen, Norway
Background: Exposure bans have a long latency.
Methods: Registry trend analysis 1980-2024 with joinpoint regression.
Results: Incidence peaked in 2012 and has fallen by 2.6% per year since.
Conclusions: The peak lags the national ban by roughly 30 years.

Title: Smoking cessation after a lung cancer diagnosis: a cohort study of 1,842 patients
Authors: Dæmi B; Exempel L; Eksempel P
Methods: Cohort with self-reported smoking status at diagnosis and 12 months.
Results: 41% of smokers had quit at 12 months; quitting was more common after curative treatment.
Conclusions: Cessation support is offered inconsistently at diagnosis.

Title: Completeness of stage recording in four Nordic lung cancer registries and its effect on survival comparisons between countries
Authors: Exempel Ö; Esimerkki A; Eksempel Ø
Affiliations: 1. Dept of Oncology, Example University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden
Methods: Registry audit with multiple imputation sensitivity analysis.
Results: Stage was missing for 3% to 14% of cases depending on registry.
Conclusions: Country rankings changed when missing stage was imputed.
